newsitem.title: FRANCE: Communists hold balance in new French parliament.
newsitem.headline: Communists hold balance in new French parliament.

text.p: The Communist party will hold the balance of power in France's new National Assembly, according to the official count.

With 564 of the 577 constituencies declared by 0.25 a.m. on Monday (2225 GMT Sunday), it was mathematically impossible for the Socialists, non-Communist left-wing parties and the Greens to reach the 289 seats required for an absolute majority without the Communists, Interior Ministry figures showed.

With 13 seats left to declare, the Socialists and allies had 268 seats and the ecologists seven, for a total of 275. Since 289 seats are necessary for an absolute majority, they were certain to need Communist votes.
First computer projections had suggested the non-communist left would hold an absolute majority without the Communists, with whom they were allied in the election campaign.
The Communist party won at least 38 seats, its best score since 1981.
